title: Board Foot, Cord, Cubic Foot: Lumber Volume Units
h1: Lumber volume — board foot, cord and cubic foot
description: 1 board foot = 1 ft × 1 ft × 1 in = 144 in³. 1 cord = 128 ft³ of stacked wood. Different products, different conventions.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 and category-specific ISO references

hero: Lumber does not sell by volume in metres or gallons — it sells by product-specific historical units.
body: The lumber industry uses several volume units that survive from pre-industrial measurement. Each captures a different aspect of the wood product: dimensional lumber (board foot), fuel wood (cord), and finished panel sheets by area.

> 1 board foot (bf, fbm) = 144 in³ = 2359.7 cm³
> 1 cord = 128 ft³ = 3.625 m³ (stacked, including air gaps)
> 1 face cord = 1/3 of a full cord (varies regionally)
> 1 MBF (thousand board feet) = 2.36 m³
Board foot: dimensional lumber pricing (2×4s, hardwood boards). Cord: firewood, pulp wood. Cubic foot / cubic metre: engineered lumber, plywood, industrial specification.

A deck needs 320 linear feet of 2×6. Nominal 2×6 = 1.5 × 5.5 in actual. Board feet: 320 × (1.5 × 5.5)/12 = 220 bf. At $2/bf, materials = $440. Estimate in cubic feet (220 × 144/1728 = 18.3 ft³) and the price per ft³ triples the number — same wood, different unit.
bf ≠ ft³. Cord is stacked volume, includes air. Match units to product convention.

faqs.q: Is nominal size or actual size used?
faqs.a: Board foot uses nominal size (2×6, 2×4). Actual dimensions are smaller after milling.

faqs.q: Is a 'thrown cord' the same as a full cord?
faqs.a: Thrown (loose) cord is 180 ft³ = 1.4× stacked cord — accounting for random air gaps.
